# Filter

## Summary
The shared filter verb: predicate builders every list view composes instead of re-deriving. `filterBy(items, ...predicates)` AND-composes and skips holes; `textMatch(needle, ...accessors)` is the case-insensitive "does any field mention this?" every search box wants; `oneOf(allowed, accessor)` is the chip/facet filter where an empty selection means "no filter"; `withinRange(min, max, accessor)` covers numbers and dates with open bounds. The invariant: a filter never throws on a hole — an unloaded link or empty field simply doesn't match.

## Usage
```ts
import filterBy, {
  textMatch,
  oneOf,
  withinRange,
} from '@cardstack/catalog/utils/filter';

let visible = filterBy(
  tasks,
  textMatch(query, (t) => t.title, (t) => t.details),
  oneOf(selectedTags, (t) => t.tags?.[0]?.name),
  withinRange(dueFrom, dueTo, (t) => t.dueDate),
  (t) => t.recordStatus !== 'Archived',
);
```
A list view composes these rather than writing its own; tag and status filtering over a task list is the shape they are built for.

**A range is a claim that the field has a value.** `textMatch('')` and `oneOf([])` pass everything through, so an untouched facet filters nothing. `withinRange` is deliberately different: an item whose accessor yields null or undefined is excluded even when both bounds are open, because asking for a range at all asserts the field is populated. A facet that should tolerate empties filters on presence separately.

`oneOf` compares by value, so its accessor must yield a primitive key — an id or a name, not a linked card or a Date. For a `linksToMany` facet, read the key: `(t) => t.tag?.id`.

## Non-goals
Not a query. Index-backed filtering belongs to search `filter` expressions, whose catalog surface sits beside `components/sort.gts`; this builds predicates over an array already in hand. Where a view needs both, derive them from one definition so they cannot disagree. Composition is AND-only: a consumer needing OR writes the predicate itself.

**On `specType`.** This is a plain module, not an invokable `Command`. The base `SpecType` enum is card / field / component / app / command and has no slot for a helper module, so `command` is the least wrong value — but anything enumerating command Specs to find something callable will surface this one, and it is not.
attributes.cardDescription: Predicate builders for list views — text match, one-of, within-range — composed by filterBy, where a missing field or unloaded link simply fails to match instead of throwing.
